**Reachability.** Toggling lamp $r$ acts on lamps $1$–$12$ as a tridiagonal matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with 1s on the diagonal and off-diagonals, because lamp 0 is excluded and lamp 12's neighbor 0 is ignored. Its determinant $D_n$ satisfies $D_n \equiv D_{n-1} + D_{n-2} \pmod 2$ with $D_0 = D_1 = 1$. This gives $D_{12} = 1$, so the matrix is invertible and all $2^{12}$ subsets of lamps $1$–$12$ are reachable. Solution 3's claim of rank 11 is wrong.

**Maximization.** We need $\max_T \left|\sum_{k \in T} z_k\right|$ over subsets $T \subseteq \{0,\dots,12\}$ containing 0. The unconstrained maximum over all subsets is attained by a set lying in an open half-plane. Thirteen equally spaced points fit at most 7 in an open semicircle, since 7 points span $166^\circ < 180^\circ$ and 8 span $194^\circ$. The best such set is 7 consecutive roots, with value $\sin(7\pi/13)/\sin(\pi/13)$. A 7-arc containing 0 exists (e.g. lamps $10,11,12,0,1,2,3$), so the constraint costs nothing and this is the true maximum.
